chunks: From Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: "Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe,"
But [He granted it] over those who take him as their master,"
And what is the [role of] Allah in your misguidance?"
When you say: 'We believe in Allah and what has been revealed to us'

key_terms.ضَلَالَكُمْ: Your misguidance or straying from the path
key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as a master/guardian

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Satan's authority over all believers versus those who take him as a master?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this distinction within the Shia doctrine of *Tawhid al-Af'āl*, emphasizing that Satan's authority is not absolute but contingent upon the believer's voluntary submission (*wilāyah*). This hadith underscores the practical implication of the Shahada, where true monotheism acts as a shield against satanic influence, while deviation invites his mastery, a concept central to understanding spiritual autonomy in Shia theology.
